title: MatPROV: A Provenance Graph Dataset of Material Synthesis Extracted from Scientific Literature
experiments_summary: The authors conducted experiments to evaluate the accuracy of LLM-based extraction of synthesis procedures into PROV-DM-compliant directed graphs. A ground truth dataset was created by randomly sampling 30 papers containing 44 synthesis procedures; a single domain expert manually annotated these in PROV-JSONLD format. Of the 30 papers, 25 were used as a test set and 5 were reserved as in-context examples. Three OpenAI models were evaluated: GPT-4.1 mini, GPT-4.1, and o4-mini. All models were first assessed under zero-shot prompting. Subsequently, o4-mini was further evaluated under one-shot prompting using each of the five reserved papers individually as an in-context example. Evaluation metrics included: (1) collection rate, measuring the proportion of ground truth synthesis procedures identified by the model, computed via label string similarity matching using Python's difflib.SequenceMatcher; (2) structural-level precision, recall, and F1-score, assessing correctness of extracted nodes and edges; and (3) parametric-level precision, recall, and F1-score, assessing correctness of key-value parameter pairs on correctly extracted nodes. String normalization (lowercasing, removal of special characters) and multiple acceptable ground truth variants were used to allow flexible semantic matching. Node-level and edge-level performance were also reported separately. All metrics were averaged across five runs with standard deviations. Based on the evaluation results, o4-mini with one-shot prompting using the best-performing in-context example (DOI: 10.1002/advs.201901598) was selected and applied to the full corpus of 1,616 papers to construct the MatPROV dataset. Additionally, synthesis backbone structures for thermoelectric and magnetic material subsets were constructed by computing forward co-occurrence frequencies among activity nodes across all extracted graphs, iteratively building directed sequences of high-frequency activity pairs using an empirically set frequency threshold of 25.
